Current NYRA usage supports Condition Book as the canonical North American document label. Retire the duplicate seed row and retain Conditions book as a moved variant label rather than a second Concept.
DQ is a current USTA code for Disqualified, not a separate result meaning. Retain one Disqualification Concept and move DQ to the abbreviation layer.
DH is a current USTA code for Dead Heat, not a separate result meaning. Retain one Dead heat Concept and move DH to the abbreviation layer.

The seed's defined sense is first two in exact order, which is the Exacta/straight-forecast mechanic. Generic Forecast can be ambiguous in British usage because straight and dual forecasts differ, so preserve the regional label with this scope note rather than a second mechanic Concept.
Reverse/Dual Forecast selects the first two in either order, matching the Quinella mechanic. Preserve the regional labels without retaining a duplicate wager Concept.

Tricast/Tierce select the first three in exact order, matching the Trifecta mechanic in the cited international/Hong Kong mapping. Preserve the regional labels rather than duplicate the wager mechanic.

Program is the American spelling/label for the programme-document sense already modeled by MEET-012. Racecard-specific document semantics remain separately modeled by MEET-011; retire the duplicate seed Concept and preserve Program as a regional label.

Current USTA chart calls use X = Break for the harness gait-break event already modeled as Broke stride. Preserve Break as a North American harness label rather than a second semantic Concept; keep RUN-002 Break separately for the Flat start-event sense.

Equibase explicitly equates the generic speed-horse/front-runner/pacesetter role. Retire the duplicate generic Pacesetter Concept into Front-runner; tactical pacemaker for another runner remains separately modeled as RUN-046.

Current Racing Australia material uses tempo for the pace of a race, while Pace already models the race/segment speed dimension. Preserve Tempo as a regional/general label rather than a duplicate semantic Concept.

Equibase uses closing kick for late acceleration and The Jockey Club defines Turn Of Foot as closing-stage acceleration ability. Preserve Kick/closing kick as colloquial or regional labels under Turn of foot rather than a second acceleration Concept.
